info.syllabusName: PRINCIPLES OF ANIMATION_Nguyên lý chuyển động
info.description:
Description:
This course takes you through the key principles of animation, which covers the '12 Principles of Animations' including: Squash & Stretch, Timing & Spacing, Solid Drawing, Anticipation, Follow Through & Overlapping Action, Arcs, Slow in & Slow out, Straight Ahead & Pose to Pose Animation, Secondary Action, Staging, Exaggeration, Appeal. This course will also provides a series of accompanying exercises to reinforce the knowledge of animation principles, including stop-motions, timelapse, flip books, etc...
Objective:
· Understand the 12 principles of Animations
· Know how to apply the 12 principles of motion to a variety of fields including 2D Animation, 3D Animation, Interactive Media, Communication Design.
· Complete an animation flipbook or paperless animation.
· Complete a short Pixilation clip.
· Complete a stop-motion clip

Apply the 12 principles of animation to various contexts, including 2D animation, stop-motion animation, and pixilation.
Complete an animation flipbook or paperless animation.

assessments.gradingGuide:
- Assessment Regulations

+ Assignments are first displayed and evaluated by students, then formally assessed and graded by the lecturer.

+ Students will receive guidance and support from the lecturer throughout the process.

-AI Usage Regulations

+ Students are allowed to use any generative AI tools to search for secondary data and generate ideas. However, they must independently construct the final product in accordance with the conditions and requirements of the assignment.

+ Students must submit an AI usage report describing the process, including screenshots that illustrate the steps taken.
assessments.note:

Tools: Can be done on paper or with graphic software such as Adobe Photoshop, Krita, etc.

2. Produce layout animation and key frames.

Tools: Hand-drawn on Flipbook paper or A5–A6 paper.

3. Draw inbetweens to complete the animation product.

Tools: Hand-drawn on Flipbook paper or A5–A6 paper.

4. Students present their work for instructor’s feedback and grading.
